TowerTorch: a fully revamped, modern UI for your Unraid server

Your server's UI on fire. Your disks stay cool.

   

What is this?

An Unraid plugin that gives your whole server a fully revamped, modern interface, without replacing a single page. Dashboard, Main, Shares, Docker, Plugins, VMs and Settings get one clean, consistent look: tiles or lists, cards with switches instead of checkboxes, small animated pictures for the disks, the array and the mover, one accent colour or a rainbow, light and dark. Everything stays where Unraid put it, so nothing you know moves.

Underneath, it looks after your containers: a start plan starts each one only once the container it depends on is actually ready, not merely "running", with per-container limits, a watchdog and schedules on top. A small Go daemon on a local unix socket does the work; nothing leaves your server.

Highlights

  • Start plan: dependency-ordered, readiness-gated start stages, so an app waits until its database is really ready. The plan window draws each container's chain lighting up in start order.
  • Readiness probes: running (with grace), TCP port, HTTP, log-line match or a command inside the container, with per-node failure policies (abort dependents, continue, or degrade)
  • Watchdog and schedules: auto-restart on crash or unhealthy (rate-capped per hour) and start, stop or restart at fixed times, per weekday
  • Idle auto-stop (inspired by ContainerNursery): stop a container after it stays idle on both CPU and network; busy and host-network containers are skipped
  • Live resource limits: CPU limit, CPU pinning (topology-aware, with P/E-core detection on Intel hybrid CPUs) and RAM limit via docker update, no restart
  • Bandwidth limits: per-container upload and download caps applied inside the container's own network namespace; the editor reads the live rule back, so a silent no-op cannot happen
  • Tiles everywhere: Docker, Main, Shares, Plugins and VMs as lists or tiles; disk tiles only mention SMART, errors and rates when there is something to say
  • Small pictures: the array's fill level as a vessel, platters that turn while a disk works, data flowing through SSDs, the mover and a parity check drawn while they run, all following your motion setting
  • Theming: one accent colour or a rainbow, light and dark, shapes and motion levels, and a master switch that turns all theming off and keeps only the orchestration
  • Local only: a small Go daemon on a local unix socket, installed as an Unraid plugin (.plg)

Requirements / Install

Install TowerTorch from Apps (Community Applications), or by URL under Plugins → Install Plugin:

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/junkerderprovinz/towertorch/main/plugin/towertorch.plg

Coming from CannonadeCommand? Install TowerTorch once the same way. It takes over your settings, start plans and limits and removes the old plugin.

  • Unraid 6.10 or newer
  • Docker, and optionally the VM manager for the VMs page
  • No reverse proxy needed: the UI is served by Unraid and the engine listens on a local unix socket

Posting a bug report

The easiest way: open Settings → Utilities → TowerTorch → Info and press Bug report. TowerTorch saves a file with the versions, your settings and start plan and the end of the engine log, with passwords and other secrets taken out. Attach it to your post or to a GitHub issue, together with:

  • The page and the action you were on (for example Docker → bandwidth gear → save)
  • Browser and operating system
  • A screenshot, if it is about how something looks

GitHub issues are just as welcome: github.com/junkerderprovinz/towertorch/issues

Credits

Built in Go for Unraid. The idle auto-stop is inspired by ContainerNursery. If TowerTorch lights up your Unraid, you can buy me a coffee.
